title: SSE probe-reset interactions causing truncated final tokens; introduce final-sentinel+checksum and probe-alignment
creator: Maya Chen
description: Several enterprise customers reported deterministic truncation of final tokens during SSE streaming sessions. Symptoms include: client receives partial last word (e.g., '...contin') and the stream unexpectedly closes with no final event; some clients observe a duplicated short suffix after reconnect. Initial triage showed no obvious server-side exception and application-level logs indicated the generator completed and committed a final chunk. Hypothesis: interaction between our short application-level SSE probe pacing and aggressive TCP reset behavior in cloud-side middleboxes causes RSTs at chunk boundaries when using chunked transfer encoding and delayed write-coalescing. This leaves the client with the last in-flight bytes dropped, then resume attempts hit a resumed-session handshake mismatch causing duplicate suffixes on reparsed partial frames.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use a reproducible text-generation prompt that ends with a non-whitespace token (e.g., 'Finish this sentence: The future of inference is')
2) Configure a test client that connects via SSE to hosted API endpoint with default keepalive (30s) and disables automatic chunk reassembly (simulate some mobile/web clients)
3) Introduce an intermediary that truncates/forcibly closes TCP when a connection is quiescent for 8-12s (simulate aggressive proxy)
4) Stream generation to completion, observe client receives truncated final token and connection ends with no explicit error
5) Reconnect and attempt resume; observe either duplicate suffix or server rejects resume depending on timing
investigation_notes: 2025-03-10 09:12: customer 'Acme Payments' escalated SEV1 after losing final token on high-value transcript exports

Captured pcap shows final TCP FIN/RST immediately following an otherwise normal data segment; server write buffers show a completed 'final' SSE event but a delay in the kernel flush coincided with proxy RST
Service logs show successful model completion events with 'final_chunk_committed' timestamp earlier than connection close; no application exception recorded

Comparison with Dedicated stack: dedicated instances using internal LB (no external proxy) do not reproduce; Private deployments sometimes reproduce when customers use older on-prem proxies with short idle timeouts
Attempted temporary mitigation by increasing client retry/backoff produced inconsistent behaviour and caused duplicate final tokens in ~12% of reproductions
root_cause: A race between our SSE end-of-stream flush timing and aggressive intermediary TCP resets. When the server defers the final socket flush (due to write coalescing or kernel buffer scheduling) and a middlebox enforces a short idle timeout, the TCP connection is reset before the client receives the trailing bytes. The resume handshake did not include a deterministic final-sentinel checksum, so resumption logic could both miss the dropped bytes or replay overlapping tokens, yielding truncated or duplicated final output.
mitigation_plan: Short-term (hotfix): Emit an explicit SSE 'final-sentinel' event with a monotonic sequence id and a short 32-bit checksum of final payload immediately before closing; perform an explicit socket-level flush and track per-connection outstanding bytes so we can correlate dropped tails in telemetry

Immediate config change: Lower our SSE application-level idle probe interval to 12s (from 30s) during canary to keep the connection active across middlebox timers, and add a server-side Nagle-friendly write mode to force immediate final buffer flush for events marked as final

Resume handshake change: include final-sentinel id and checksum in resume request and server-side resume verification; on checksum mismatch, server should veto resume and return 'resume_reject' with canonical reason instead of attempting best-effort replay

Customer mitigation guidance: provide customers with a recommended gateway/proxy idle timeout of >= 30s or to pass-through SSE traffic; provide sample client logic for verifying final-sentinel checksum when reconnecting
long_term_changes: Introduce per-session end-to-end checksums for SSE sessions (optional opt-in with versioning), extend our streaming contract to include atomic final events, and implement server-side early detect+abort when kernel flush latencies exceed threshold
Add network-level synthetic tests (chaos tests) that simulate proxy resets during tail chunks and validate final-sentinel behaviour on CI for hosted runtime and dedicated/private variants
Enhance telemetry: per-connection sequence id, final-sentinel checksum, server-flush-latency histogram and proxy-reset detection tags; alert when proxy-resets per 1k streams exceed 0.5%
rollout_plan: 1) Implement final-sentinel + checksum + resume verification behind feature flag on runtime:feature/sse-final-sentinel
2) Canary rollout to 5% of hosted traffic for two days while monitoring user-visible truncations and duplicate-token regressions
3) If canary looks stable, ramp to 50% over 48 hours, then 100% in 48 hours, coordinate with Dedicated/Private teams for parallel opt-in (Private customers require upgrade window)
4) If checksum mismatch rate > 0.1% or flakiness observed, rollback automatically and open critical incident
acceptance_criteria: 1) Hosted production canary shows >= 90% reduction in reported truncated final-token customer incidents for the canary cohort
2) No measurable increase in duplicate final-token occurrences compared to baseline (<= 0.05% change),
3) Telemetry fields (final_sent_id, final_checksum, flush_latency_ms) are populated for 99% of SSE sessions in canary
4) Client resume path returns deterministic 'accepted' or 'resume_reject' which client SDKs can handle; sample SDK release published with resume-checksum verification
5) Dedicated and Private deployment guides updated with explicit proxy/gateway recommendations and a toggle for the final-sentinel feature
